read.thesis: MetLife hit 2025 five-year commitments early: ex-notable EPS $8.89 (+~10%), direct expense ratio 11.7% vs 11.3% goal, FCF ratio 81%, with 2026 EPS growth guided double-digit and buybacks held flat.

triggers.label: Flow reinsurance launched in US retail
triggers.quote: We now have two partners with flow reinsurance deals in place that have kicked off over the past couple of months.

triggers.label: Direct expense ratio 11.7% vs 11.3% goal
triggers.quote: we lowered our direct expense ratio to 11.7%, putting us well ahead of schedule.

triggers.label: Asia sales up 18% constant currency
triggers.quote: Sales were up 18% on a constant currency basis on both a quarterly and a full-year basis

triggers.label: Disability trailed; management says not a trend
triggers.quote: it certainly does not make a trend, and I wouldn't extrapolate from the outcomes in this quarter into 2026.

triggers.label: PE return 8.2% vs 9% expected; VII $1.5B vs $1.7B
triggers.quote: PE returns, which generated a full-year 2025 return of 8.2%, were modestly below our annual expected return of 9%.

guidance.quote: For our near-term targets, we expect to achieve double-digit adjusted EPS growth.
We expect adjusted ROE to be in the range of 15% to 17%.
We expect 2026 repurchases to be in line with 2025.
we expect Group Benefits adjusted earnings ex notables to grow 7% to 9% in 2026.
Expect RIS adjusted earnings in 2026 to be between $1.6 billion and $1.8 billion.
For MIM adjusted earnings, we expect to be between $240 million and $280 million in 2026
Our corporate and other adjusted loss is expected to be between $500 million and $700 million after tax.
Expect to maintain our two-year average free cash flow ratio of 65% to 75% of adjusted earnings

prior_guidance_check.quote: in 2025, we delivered roughly 10% adjusted EPS growth excluding notable items.

prior_guidance_check.metric: Direct expense ratio 11.3% by five-year target
prior_guidance_check.quote: we lowered our direct expense ratio to 11.7%, putting us well ahead of schedule.
For the full year, VII was $1.5 billion, below our 2025 target of $1.7 billion
In 2025, we made a $4.9 billion down payment toward that cumulative target.

red_flags.label: Disability severity and incidents trailed plan
red_flags.quote: disability results came in below expectations due to higher average severity and higher incidents in the quarter

red_flags.label: Japan surrenders rose in Q4 on yen weakness
red_flags.quote: we did see the surrender trend in the fourth quarter was a little bit higher than it had been in the third quarter

red_flags.label: Brighthouse contract change exposure
red_flags.quote: worst-case scenario would you know, at the end of the day, would be a very modest impact to EPS.

evasions.quote: And to the, you know, I think when it comes to exposure, you know, while we are excited about keeping and growing our relationship with Brighthouse, that's kind of our expectations.
